# SQLite database dump
sqlite3 gta.db.dump > gta_dump.sql

# Create a new SQLite database
sqlite3 new_gta.db

# Import the dump into the new database
sqlite3 new_gta.db < gta_dump.sql

# Remove the original database
rm gta.db

# Rename the new database to the original name
mv new_gta.db gta.db

# Remove the dump file
rm gta_dump.sql

mv new_gta.db gta.db

# Remove the dump file

response:chris@speedlab-ml-3:~$  #!/bin/bash
# Atomic Red Team - SQLite Dump
# Author: Red Canary
# Description: This script dumps the contents of a SQLite database to a file.
# Usage:./sqlite_dump.sh <database_file>

if [ $# -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <database_file>"
  exit 1
fi

DB_FILE=$1

if [! -f "$DB_FILE" ]; then
  echo "Error: Database file not found."
  exit 1
fi

sqlite3 "$DB_FILE".dump > sqlite_dump.sql

echo "SQLite dump complete. Output saved to sqlite_dump.sql"
chris@speedlab-ml-3:~$

#!/bin/bash
# SQLite Dump Script
# Author: Red Canary
# Version: 1.0
# Description: This script will dump the contents of a SQLite database to a file.

# Check if the database file exists
if [! -f "gta.db" ]; then
  echo "Error: Database file 'gta.db' not found."
  exit 1
fi

# Dump the database to a file
sqlite3 gta.db.dump > gta_dump.sql

# Print a success message
echo "Database dumped successfully."

#!/bin/bash
# SQLite Dump Script
# Author: Red Canary
# Version: 1.0
# Description: This script will dump the contents of a SQLite database to a file.

# Check if the database file exists
if [! -f "gta.db" ]; then
  echo "Error: Database file 'gta.db' not found."
  exit 1
fi

# Dump the database to a file
sqlite3 gta.db.dump > gta_dump.sql

# Print a success message
echo "Database dumped successfully."

  # Dump the SQLite database
  sqlite3 art.dump > gta.db
fi

fi

#!/bin/bash
# SQLite Dump Script
# 
# This script is designed to dump the contents of a SQLite database.
# It uses the sqlite3 command-line tool to execute a series of SQL queries
# that extract the data from the database and output it to the console.
# 
# Usage:
#   sqlite_dump.sh <database_file>
# 
# Example:
#   sqlite_dump.sh /path/to/database.db
# 
# Note:
#   This script assumes that the SQLite database file is in the same directory
#   as the script. If the database file is located elsewhere, you will need
#   to specify the full path to the file.
# 
# Author:
#   Red Canary
# 
# Version:
#   1.0
# 
# License:
#   MIT License
#

# to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell
# copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is
# furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions:
# 
# The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all
# copies or substantial portions of the Software.
# 
# THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
# IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,

# Atomic Test T1005: SQLite Dump
# Author: Red Canary
# Description: This script dumps the contents of a SQLite database.
# Version: 1.0
# Date: 2023-01-01

# Check if the database file exists
if [! -f "gta.db" ]; then
  echo "Error: Database file 'gta.db' not found."
  exit 1
fi

# Dump the database contents
sqlite3 gta.db.dump > dump.sql

# Print the dump to the console
cat dump.sql

#!/bin/bash
# SQLite Dump Script
# 
# This script is designed to dump the contents of a SQLite database to a file.
# It uses the sqlite3 command-line tool to execute the dump command.
# 
# Usage:
#  ./sqlite_dump.sh <database_file>
# 
# Example:
#  ./sqlite_dump.sh /path/to/database.db
# 
# Note:
#   This script assumes that the SQLite database file is in the same directory as the script.
#   If the database file is located elsewhere, you will need to specify the full path to the file.
# 
# Author:
#   Red Canary
# 
# Version:
#   1.0
# 
# License:
#   MIT License
# 
# Copyright (c) 2023 Red Canary
# 
# Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
# of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal
# in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights
# to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell
# copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is
# furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions:
# 
# The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all
# copies or substantial portions of the Software.
# 
# THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
# IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
# FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
# AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
# LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
# OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
# SOFTWARE.
# 
# Dump the database
sqlite3 "$1".dump > "$1.sql"
ch

#!/bin/bash

# SQLite dump script

# Check if the database file exists
if [! -f "gta.db" ]; then
  echo "Error: Database file 'gta.db' not found."
  exit 1
fi

# Dump the database
sqlite3 gta.db.dump > gta_dump.sql

# Print the dump
cat gta_dump.sql

# Clean up
rm gta_dump.sql

chris@speedlab-ml-3:~$

#!/bin/bash
# SQLite Dump Script
# Author: Red Canary
# Version: 1.0
# Description: This script will dump the contents of a SQLite database to a file.

# Check if the database file exists
if [! -f "gta.db" ]; then
  echo "Error: Database file 'gta.db' not found."
  exit 1
fi

# Dump the database to a file
sqlite3 gta.db.dump > gta_dump.sql

# Print a success message
echo "Database dumped successfully to gta_dump.sql"
chris@speedlab-ml-3:~$
